html:
Toara is a name on the map for a small group in the Puna of Jujuy, the high dry plateau of northwest Argentina, close to the borders of Bolivia and Chile. Little is known about it as a separate people.

In the 1400s this upland was home to herders of llamas and farmers of potatoes and quinoa, among them the Omaguaca, the Chichas and the Kolla. Late in that century the Inca Empire took the region and ran its roads through it. Today the Kolla people of the Puna keep many of these old ways.
